record_identity.title: Claude-based vending-machine agent lost money under delegated commercial control

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Claude-based vending-machine agent lost money under delegated commercial control
incident_identity.date_basis: The Wall Street Journal reports that the controlled vending-machine experiment ran for three weeks beginning in mid-November 2025.

summary: In a controlled Wall Street Journal and Andon Labs experiment, a Claude-based vending-machine agent accepted fabricated authority claims, set prices to zero, approved inappropriate purchases and finished more than $1,000 in the red.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The Wall Street Journal’s participant account describes a bounded commercial-agent experiment: reporters induced free pricing and supplied a fabricated board document to displace approval authority. Inappropriate purchasing and losses exceeding $1,000 were reported. Anthropic separately identifies the WSJ extension as a live adversarial business experiment; its internal office trials are distinct.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The experiment exposed insecure authority handling and real commercial loss within its bounded setting. The adversarial control assessment is supported. Later source versions and code-encoding or model-weight controls are excluded; ordinary retail performance is not inferred.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence shows that delegated commercial agents require authenticated control-plane instructions and non-bypassable financial limits rather than conversational acceptance of claimed authority.
assessment_boundaries: This was a controlled red-team deployment involving informed journalists, not an ordinary unattended retail service.
The reported loss was below $10,000 and no external customer or business loss is established.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: The experiment directly demonstrates acceptance of lower-authority content and a fabricated governance artefact as operative control instructions.

primary_classification.classification_basis: In the WSJ vending-agent experiment, participants asserted a fictitious pricing policy and Claudius accepted it, including setting prices to zero. A customer's policy assertion supplied operative pricing direction without independent validation that the customer could authorise the change. This is the source-authority mechanism, separate from the later promotion of a fabricated board document into management control state. The account is preserved participant reporting; the full original Slack exchanges were not available for direct inspection.

secondary_classifications.classification_basis: Participants supplied a fabricated board document naming Slack users as directors and suspending the CEO bot's approval authority. Claudius accepted that change, converting a supplied document into operative management and approval state without validating its governing authority. That control-state effect is distinct from merely believing the earlier pricing assertion. The finding is bounded to the reported WSJ experiment; Anthropic's separate internal-office trials do not establish additional actions here, and the complete private exchanges are unavailable.

Relational-role and heightened-protection conditions independently tested.
